answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, select players+1 face-down, place them on the board and return the rest unseen; put one random structure bonus tile face-up below Popularity; place encounter tokens on 11 marked territories. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards; structure bonus tile; 11 marked territories; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: On the map: each player’s character starts at home base and two workers start on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it. On mats: four mechs over faction abilities, six stars by faction emblem, six cubes in black-square green boxes, four structures in matching boxes, four recruits in bottom-row circles, remaining six workers on Produce red rectangles, and action token beside Player Mat ready for first placement; one-time recruit spaces stay empty. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards.

You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action (a dead turn), either action, or both; if both, top must precede bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, but top and bottom actions each remain once per turn. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing any amount of exposed green-box benefit; benefits may be declined, and exact costs/benefits are mat-dependent.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section; full cost; optional benefit; Rusviet limit.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls the territory and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure’s abilities; you retain the abilities even without control, except your Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled. You may pay with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.

No: normal Move selects up to two different units and moves each one adjacent territory; the same unit cannot use both selections. A transported worker’s carriage does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself. All unit types may carry any number of resources; only mechs may carry any number of your workers, and never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins; carrying and movement.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech entering enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero (zero popularity does not prevent retreat). This is not combat. A worker cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs; the summary does not specifically state a rule barring your worker from entering a territory controlled only by enemy workers in this situation.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers only; worker entry restrictions.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: characters/mechs; Combat; worker movement restriction.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power OR one combat card, before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards to form a deck, and if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) OR one popularity, before upgrades. Place traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; built Armory adds one power to Trade.

Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production, then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one terrain-matching token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.

Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat (varies by mat/upgrades); move a cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Deploy costs the exposed Deploy cost-box number of metal tokens (also mat/upgrades dependent); put a mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and all your mechs, not workers. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for the bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade; Deploy; completed bottom action.

answers.answer: Build any of your structures on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total per territory, and lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. Mill gives a bonus Produce territory only while you control it; it cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Mine is your personal tunnel for your units even while enemy units occupy its territory, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions. Enemy units do not gain your structure abilities.

Take a recruit from any bottom-row section, place it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat, and immediately gain that space’s two power, two coins, two popularity or two combat cards. Its ongoing bonus is instead the circle uncovered where you removed it: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. On a triggered action resolve active player, then immediate left, then immediate right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.

Both combatants simultaneously and secretly set dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven or current power, and may add up to one card per participating character/mech (Rusviet adds one total if workers are present). If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each player deducts selected dial power from the Power Track; played cards are discarded face-up, with no extra track power deduction for card values.

Loser’s characters, mechs and workers all retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy can instead send eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; a winning defender loses none, with Polania Camaraderie’s stated exception. Non-Saxony winner places a combat star if they have zero or one combat stars, and none if already at two; Saxony places one after every victory while star tokens remain. A loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.

After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter only if the character remains there; if it loses contested entry, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains go to the encounter territory. Pay the card’s printed cost, but no normal action cost applies and no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses are gained.

Every player’s character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one and returns the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. Factory card works as a fifth section, with optional top then bottom subject to usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); it gives no matching Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or character/mech up to three with Speed, under normal movement restrictions; Mine access applies.

Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; all requirements must be met at reveal, though you may wait to reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the deck bottom. Normally only one objective star; Saxony keeps its second card after the first and may score both.

Stars are awarded for six upgrades, four mechs deployed, four structures built, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Goals are each awarded once except combat’s two-star allowance and Saxony’s exception; another player’s star does not block the goal. A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later falls. The sixth star immediately ends play with no equalizing turns or further actions.

If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing the star. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish active action, then check active player, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for game end each time; if earlier player places sixth star, later neighbor star/bonus does not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement and return initiating units; do not resolve another combat.

At 10 popularity, use the 7–12 tier: $4 per star, $3 per territory count and $2 per complete resource pair. Thus five stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory count as 7, adding $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs, adding $12; total addition to held coins before structure bonus is $53. Selected structure bonus scores from your structures even if enemies control those territories. Tiebreaks: workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune; current popularity tiers; Factory counts 3; structure bonus eligibility; tie order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory. Normally units cannot move back into a home base, nor may you build or deploy there; setup, forced retreats and Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.

Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, village a worker; lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. There is no supply limit for resource tokens; use multipliers if needed.

Any unit may pick up, carry and drop resources during movement; a mech can pick up/drop workers mid-movement too. Mechs carry your workers, never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers; tunnel jump costs one step, so extra step may be before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
Any unit can enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat; thus workers can capture it. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.

You may not pay a partial cost. If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn: move your token to a different section and take neither action. After last using Move, this allows a legal turn by moving to another section and taking neither action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: dead turn; full cost.

answers.answer: Built Armory grants +1 power on Trade; built Monument grants +1 popularity on Bolster. These trigger on those top actions. You keep structure abilities even without control, except Mill production; enemy units do not gain your abilities, so an enemy occupant does not take away the Armory/Monument benefits.

Riverwalk for character/mechs only: Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is instead for workers alone to cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; it does not help Nordic character/mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities table.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts are for characters/mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass; Township.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: opponent loses two power on track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery also applies before combat, but you pay one power to reduce opponent power by two; once per combat, not per unit.

With at least one worker present, Rusviet People’s Army permits one additional combat card total; with two mechs and three workers, those two mechs can play three cards total. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech must participate.

Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot enter an active opponent’s home base.

Crimea Scout steals one random combat card from opponent into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion is once per turn: spend one combat card as any one resource, regardless of its value.

Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge permits character/mechs to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; it does not give Polania the Nordic adjacent-lake retreat exception. When lake-capable carrier leaves, workers on the lake require a mech to move off; carried workers or resources cannot be left behind on a lake.

Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not protect against popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.

Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay the second option’s cost. Pay each selected option’s printed cost and may take as little of its benefit as desired; gains go to encounter territory.

Character entering encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including Factory Move. Resolve encounter after the whole Move action and all combats, and only if the character remains there.

Coins are not hidden, but you need not reveal their exact total when asked. Combat card hand count is public, except during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.

Informal agreements are unenforceable; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). Negotiation/payment cannot cancel combat once movement has put units onto opposing units; fight after Move, though bribes may influence outcome.

Popularity 0–6: $3/star, $2/territory count, $1/complete resource pair. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, $3. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Resources score only in complete pairs, so an odd leftover single scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and scoring rules.

answers.answer: For adjacency tiles, each feature is counted once across all your structures. Rivers do not break adjacency. Tunnel tile counts unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; encounter tile counts unique printed encounter locations even if token removed; lake tile counts unique lakes. Payout for each tile: 1=$2; 2–3=$4; 4–5=$6; 6=$9 for tunnels, and 6–7=$9 for lakes/encounters; zero scores zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table; adjacency notes.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row counts only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras counts combined qualifying structures: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; Polania Camaraderie may provide the stated exception.

No. A placed star is permanent, but current popularity still determines final scoring. The summary says goals are awarded once for each player and another player’s star never blocks a goal, so two factions may each place a star for the same achievement.

Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania clockwise, omitting inactive factions. This matters because recruit bonuses trigger for you, your immediate left and right neighbors when they take matching bottom actions.

A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
You may not keep the drawn encounter card private: show it to all players, show its artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain. Interactive bonuses and game-end priority resolve in order.

No. In a turn each section’s top and bottom actions are each limited to once, including Rusviet; taking bottom means you cannot return to top. Rusviet repeat waives only the different-section-from-last-turn restriction, not within-turn limits.
You may choose the alternative Move benefit and gain $1, before upgrades.
No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; retreat sends them to home base, not to the mat.
Yes. You may attack with zero power and/or zero popularity.
Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places no further combat star.

A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose any. It cannot choose unaffordable coin/popularity options. It may take as little of the chosen benefit as desired.
No turn-order selection: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power and cards. They reveal simultaneously after selection.
Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

No. Place a star as soon as you achieve its goal; the sixth ends the game immediately. Objective is the exception: you may wait to reveal a completed objective, and requirements must all hold when you reveal it.
Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions. A river is a border between land territories, while lake occupies a hex.
No. The recruit is put permanently on a one-time recruit bonus space and cannot later move.
No. Only a character triggers an encounter; it stops on entering the token territory, and encounter is resolved if it remains there after combats.

While controlled, Mill gives one bonus production territory in addition to the normal selected territories: up to 3 instead of 2, or up to 4 with upgraded allowance of 3. Mill itself counts as one producing worker and produces its terrain’s token even with no actual worker there; each actual worker at the Mill can also produce normally, so Mill output is additive.

You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there and no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control; after your last unit leaves a territory without your structure, you do not control it. An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it.
Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
